description: Use Claude Code in your pytests, or pytest your own Claude Code agents — or both
rules: Use the claude_client fixture (a SpyClaudeSDKClient) only when the code under test accepts a Claude client via dependency injection; if it calls claude_agent_sdk.query() directly, use unittest.mock.patch or pytest-mock instead.

Three fixtures are registered automatically: claude_query (raw query function), claude_client (recording spy for the app under test), claude_judge_client (separate query function for LLM-as-judge assertions).
Keep the app under test and the test oracle apart: drive the app with claude_client and grade its output with claude_judge_client.
Every fixture call is an async generator: combine @pytest.mark.asyncio with `async for msg in ...`, and read the final text from the ResultMessage via msg.result.
SpyClaudeSDKClient needs no connect()/disconnect() — each query() call opens its own connection, passes the call through to the real LLM, and records it.
Assert on recorded calls with assert_called(), assert_not_called(), assert_called_once(), assert_call_count(n), assert_any_call_contains(text), assert_last_call_contains(text), and reset_calls().

Inspect recorded calls directly through claude_client.calls (list of CallRecord), claude_client.call_count and claude_client.last_call; each CallRecord exposes prompt, kwargs, response and the result shortcut.
Pass ClaudeAgentOptions as the options keyword argument, e.g. claude_client.query(prompt, options=ClaudeAgentOptions(max_turns=1)); it is stored in CallRecord.kwargs for assertions.
Mark every test that makes a real LLM call with @pytest.mark.llm so CI can run `pytest -m 'not llm'` for a fast pass and `pytest -m llm` for the costly one.
Real LLM responses vary between runs, so ask for deterministic, checkable output (e.g. "Answer only YES or NO") and assert on that rather than on exact wording.
Authentication uses the logged-in Claude Code CLI by default; set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for pay-as-you-go API billing, or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 for cloud providers.
